summary: Stream session unexpectedly resets after backend KV-cache migration causing mid-response disconnects
description:
Issue summary:
Customer FinFlow reports streaming chat sessions (SSE) disconnecting mid-generation after a scheduled KV-cache migration ran during a maintenance window. Impact: several in-flight streaming responses for premium enterprise accounts terminated with a 499/connection reset on the client.

Impact:
- ~12 user sessions affected over a 35-minute window during migration (est. 80 requests).
- Client-visible symptom: stream closes with no final [DONE] event and no error payload; client sees connection reset or EOF.
- Business impact: delayed or missing invoice summaries in customer app; escalated to account team.

Environment:
- prod-us-east, dedicated enterprise route for FinFlow (enterprise routing policy).
- Model: redwood-open-7b-v2 pinned.
- Route: streaming chat endpoint with SSE proxy and per-tenant cache slicing.

Steps to reproduce (customer-reported):
1) Start a long-generation chat (context length ~16k tokens, expected multi-minute response).
2) During generation, wait ~5-20 minutes; migration started by platform during that period.
3) SSE connection either drops with TCP RST on client or remains silent and then closes.

Observed behavior:
- Server-side logs show worker continued generation for a short period after upstream events, then session record removed and connection closed by proxy.
- No generation completion event emitted to client.
- Traces show a short window where KV-cache shard reassignment happened and the router re-evaluated routing policy for the tenant.

Expected behavior:
- Long-running streaming sessions should remain connected and continue generation unaffected by background cache migration. If failover is required, server should emit a structured error and attempt graceful handoff to fallback worker.

Relevant logs (sanitized):
- proxy: [2026-03-10T07:12:43Z] conn=fd-41234 tenant=finflow session=se-88d3 keepalive=120
- router: [2026-03-10T07:12:45Z] routing:evict-slice tenant=finflow shard=us-east-3 reason=kv-shard-migrate
- serving-runtime: [2026-03-10T07:12:46Z] worker=wr-71 in-progress=session=se-88d3 model=redwood-open-7b-v2 tokens_generated=842
- proxy: [2026-03-10T07:12:48Z] conn=fd-41234 error=upstream_reset by=router code=RST
- client: EOF / websocket close 1006 (no final chunk)

Attachments:
- trace ids: trace-9c4b2a (proxy->router->worker), tcp dump (redacted) attached by customer.

Additional notes:
- Customer reports issue coincided exactly with our KV-cache shard migration scheduled at 07:12 UTC. They observed the interruption only on long streaming responses; short responses unaffected.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:05 - Support (Ava Thompson): Opened ticket after initial customer report. Collected traces, tcpdump, and sample session IDs. Escalating to SRE and runtime team.

2026-03-10 09:15 - SRE (Ravi Patel): Confirmed shard migration task ran at 07:12 UTC; observed router emitting evict-slice for tenant finflow. Noted proxy issued connection RST soon after. Investigating session lifecycle on cache reassignment.

2026-03-10 11:40 - Runtime Eng (Laila Gomez): Hypothesis: during shard migration we prematurely remove session metadata which the proxy uses to keep route sticky; worker continues generation but proxy closes socket when session lookup fails. Adding metrics to detect session deletions during active generations.
2026-03-11 02:20 - Support (Ava Thompson): Customer accepted temporary workaround to disable scheduled migration for their tenant; they requested a formal incident report and corrective-action ETA.

2026-03-12 14:05 - SRE (Ravi Patel): Patch created to make cache migration drain sessions gracefully (PR linked). Will coordinate canary rollout in staging then prod. Informing customer of timeline: staged rollout starting 2026-03-13.
2026-03-12 16:30 - Account Exec (Maya Chen): Notified FinFlow of next steps and temporary credit being issued for affected requests.
investigation_notes: Initial correlation shows eviction event (router:evict-slice) triggers session-index cleanup before in-flight worker emits final tokens. The proxy relies on the session index to validate keepalive and route continuity; once index entry removed, proxy issues RST. Reproduced in internal staging by forcing concurrent migration during long-stream generation. Root cause: migration path did an unconditional delete of session index entries instead of marking them draining. Also uncovered a gap where worker-generated final events are not re-queued if proxy disconnects mid-chunk.
resolution_notes:
Temporary mitigation: disabled scheduled KV-cache migration for FinFlow tenant during maintenance window and advised customers to re-run interrupted requests. Long-term fix implemented in serving-runtime and router:
1) Change migration workflow to mark session index entries as draining and delay deletion until active generation count reaches zero or timeout.
2) Proxy change: when session lookup fails for an active connection, hold connection for 30s while attempting reconfirmation with router; do not immediately close.
3) Worker change: emit final generation chunk to durable event queue so proxy can replay on reconnection within short window.

Status: Patch submitted (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1293 and router PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/774). Staged canary in us-east-1 scheduled 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC. Post-canary, will roll to prod with telemetry enabled to verify reduced mid-stream disconnects.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem to SRE channel and Confluence page (assigned to Ravi).
- Add automated test to CI that simulates migration during long streaming and asserts no connection resets.
- Update migration runbook to include draining semantics and tenant opt-out checklist.
resolution: Fix in progress; temporary workaround applied (migration paused for FinFlow). Canary rollout planned. Customer notified and provided temporary credits. Expected to resolve after canary completes and patch promoted to prod.
safety_and_comms: Customer notified 2026-03-10 10:30 UTC. Account team provided interim credit. Formal incident/debrief will be published on Confluence and shared with FinFlow post-rollback verification.
next_steps: 1) Run canary rollout in us-east-1 on 2026-03-13. 2) Monitor streaming disconnect rate for finflow:baseline and overall: expect >90% reduction in mid-stream disconnects for long responses. 3) Implement CI test and update runbook. 4) Close ticket after successful prod verification.
